description: We are a multidisciplinary team of creators, developers, and designers from Kyiv, driven by a passion for space exploration and tech innovation. We bridge complex space data with intuitive visual design and responsive engineering. Combining analytical depth with relentless drive, we turn complex challenges into sleek, impactful solutions for NASA Space Apps.
summary:
Orbit Architect is an interactive 2D space mission simulation game that challenges players to design, balance, and launch a scientific expedition to Mars.

Addressing the complexity of real-world aerospace engineering, the game puts players in the role of mission lead, guided by a core team of specialists—a financier, engineer, navigator, and scientist. Players assemble a rocket across four critical stages (Payload, Power Systems, Auxiliary Modules, and Launch Vehicle), selecting from 12 distinct components such as the MARS-SAR Radar, Quantum Spectrometer, and Base Drill. Every choice directly impacts real-time telemetry parameters, requiring strict balance within a $400M budget, total mass limits, and power consumption thresholds before calculating the Earth-to-Mars trajectory.

By turning intricate mission planning and resource trade-offs into an accessible, visually engaging experience, Orbit Architect bridges the gap between technical space science and interactive education.
details:
What it does & how it works

Orbit Architect is a 2D strategy and simulation game where you manage a scientific expedition to the Martian south pole. You start in a briefing room with four crew specialists—a Financier, Engineer, Navigator, and Scientist—who react to your choices and give practical hints. From there, you assemble a rocket across four stages (Payload, Power Systems, Auxiliary Modules, and Launch Vehicle), picking from 12 modules like the MARS-SAR Radar, Quantum Spectrometer, or RTG-Gold. Every part affects your $400M budget, total mass, and power balance. Once the telemetry checks out, you launch, simulate the Earth-to-Mars trajectory, and earn mission medals that unlock extra funding and power capacity for future runs.

Benefits & Impact

Aerospace engineering usually feels intimidating because of heavy math. We wanted to make systems engineering intuitive and fun: players immediately feel why a power-hungry spectrometer forces them to upgrade solar wings and switch to a heavier launch vehicle. It helps students and space fans grasp real mission trade-offs through hands-on trial and error.

Tools & Tech Stack The game was developed using Rust, JavaScript, and CSS (with PowerShell and Shell scripts for build automation), compiled to WebAssembly (WASM) so anyone can play directly in their browser via GitHub Pages without downloading anything. All 2D character sprites, emotion states, UI dashboards, and rocket modules were hand-crafted as vector graphics in Adobe Illustrator and finalized in Adobe Photoshop.

Creativity & Design Factors

Instead of dry spreadsheets, we gave the mission a human face through expressive characters and narrative tension. When balancing the game, we focused on two things: instant browser accessibility and tight mathematical balance so there is no single "winning" rocket build—every design requires real engineering compromises.
